memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: They did not dislodge the Canaanites living in Gezer; to this day the Canaanites live among the people of Ephraim but are required to do forced labor - Josh 16:10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter closes, like others before it, on an honest and sobering note. Ephraim "did not dislodge the Canaanites living in Gezer." Instead of driving them out as God had commanded, they let them remain and put them to forced labour. It seemed like a practical arrangement — useful workers, avoided conflict — but it was disobedience dressed up as convenience.

We should be honest about how tempting this kind of compromise is. Full obedience is costly; a partial arrangement often looks easier and even beneficial. Why fight a hard battle when you can strike a comfortable deal? But God had warned that the peoples left in the land would become a snare (Num 33:55). What Ephraim tolerated for convenience would, in time, pull Israel toward the very idolatry God had warned against. Sin we make peace with rarely stays quietly in its corner.

This is a searching word for us. Are there "Canaanites in Gezer" in our own lives — sins we have decided not to fight, but to manage? Habits we have put to "forced labour," telling ourselves we have them under control? The call of the gospel is not to negotiate with sin but to put it to death by the Spirit (Rom 8:13). We cannot do this in our own strength, but Christ has broken sin's power, and by His Spirit we are given grace to stop striking deals and start driving out what harms us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What sin have you chosen to manage rather than truly deal with?
- Why is a comfortable compromise often more tempting than full obedience?
- How does Christ's power over sin free you to stop negotiating with it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, forgive me for the compromises I have made peace with instead of confronting. By Your Spirit, give me grace to put to death the sins I have merely been managing. Amen.
